# The C interface: `openrac/openrac_mod.h`

The interface between OpenRAC's native port and a native mod (docs/port/MODS.md).

A mod is a shared library (.dylib, .so, .dll) that exports openrac_mod_query and openrac_mod_load,
and optionally openrac_mod_unload. The port opens it at start, before the game runs, asks
openrac_mod_query which interface it was built for, and calls openrac_mod_load with the table of
what the port offers (openrac_api). The mod uses nothing of the port but that table: it is built
against this header alone, and links against nothing of OpenRAC's.

Versions. OPENRAC_MOD_API_MAJOR changes when anything in the table changes or goes: a mod built
for another major is refused. OPENRAC_MOD_API_MINOR grows when something is added at the end of
the table: a mod built for a minor above the port's is refused, one built for a lower minor loads
(and checks api->api_minor before it uses anything newer than what it was built for).

Everything runs on the game's thread: load, the hooks, the callbacks, unload.

This header is plain C (C99, and C++ through its extern "C" block): it is the ABI, and the C++
layer (openrac/mod.hpp) is built on it. It is laid out as: versions, helper macros, types,
the input state, the table (openrac_api), the entry points, then the helpers a mod uses.
Each item says which interface version added it ("Since 1.0" is the original table); a mod
checks api->api_minor before it uses anything newer than the minor it was built for.

## Types

```c
typedef uint32_t openrac_gaddr;
```

A game address: an offset into game memory (the console's address). Since 1.0.

```c
typedef struct openrac_mod openrac_mod;
```

The port's handle for one loaded mod, passed back to the functions that are the mod's own (its
log lines, its settings, its hooks). Opaque; valid from openrac_mod_load until the program ends.
Since 1.0.

```c
typedef int (*openrac_menu_fn)(void* user, const openrac_menu_frame* frame);
```

A mod's menu page (openrac_api.menu_entry): called once a frame while the page is open, on the
game's thread, with the `user` pointer the mod gave. It draws the page with menu_rect and
menu_text (the page starts each frame black) and returns OPENRAC_MENU_STAY or
OPENRAC_MENU_CLOSE. While the page is open the game sees no button of pad 0. Since 1.5.

```c
typedef void (*openrac_ui_fn)(void* user, int page, const openrac_ui_event* event);
```

A mod's page (openrac_api.ui_page): called on the game's thread with the `user` pointer the mod
gave, the page's id and each event. The calls of the table work from here (ui_set, ui_open, ...);
what they ask for happens after the call. Since 1.7.

```c
typedef int (*openrac_moby_update_fn)(void* user, int slot, int phase);
```

The gate (openrac_api.on_moby_update): called with the `user` pointer the mod gave, before and
after the update of the moby in `slot` (not for one a mod drives). Before it, returns 1 to skip
the update (then no call after), 0 to run it. Since 1.9.

```c
typedef int (*openrac_hit_fn)(void* user, const openrac_hit* hit);
```

Told a hit the game posted (openrac_api.on_moby_hit); returns 1 to take it back (the victim
never reads it), 0 to leave it. Since 1.9.

```c
typedef void (*openrac_frame_fn)(void* user);
```

A function the port calls after each game tick (openrac_api.on_frame), with the `user` pointer
the mod gave. Since 1.0.

```c
typedef void (*openrac_tick_boundary_fn)(void* user, uint32_t tick);
```

Called after the game's vertical-blank handlers have run. Snapshot operations are only accepted
from this callback, at the port's tick boundary. Since 1.6.

```c
typedef void (*openrac_pad_fn)(void* user, int port, uint8_t* report, int size);
```

A function the port calls for each pad report (openrac_api.on_pad), with the `user` pointer the
mod gave. `report` is the report as the console's pad library hands it to the game (its bytes,
`size` of them), which the callback may change before the game reads it; `port` is the
controller's port, 0 or 1. Since 1.0.

```c
typedef void (*openrac_party_rules_fn)(void* user, const void* data, uint32_t size);
```

The host's rules for this mod reached this game (openrac_api.party_rules_deliver), `size` bytes
as the same mod published them in the host's game; null and 0 when there are none any more (the
party went): the mod's own settings count again. Since 1.11.

```c
typedef void (*openrac_overlay_fn)(void* user, const openrac_overlay* overlay);
```

Called once a frame, after the world is drawn and before the port's own overlay, while the game
shows a level (not in a menu or a scene). Since 1.12.

```c
typedef void (*openrac_camera_script_fn)(void* user, int id, int started);
```

A camera script (a door, a lift) started (`started` 1) or ended (0) in this game, `id` its number
in the level (the same in every game of that level). Since 1.12.

```c
typedef int (*openrac_metal_detect_fn)(void* user, int slot, int key);
```

The metal detector found a buried moby (`slot`, `key`) as the game was about to give its bolts.
Return non-zero to let the game go on, 0 to hold it back (the mod has asked someone else, and
tells the game of the outcome with moby_kill and bolts). Since 1.12.

```c
typedef void (*openrac_mod_query_fn)(openrac_mod_info* info);
```

Tells the port which interface the mod was built for: sets `info`'s api_major, api_minor, id and
version. Called before the mod is loaded. Required; OPENRAC_MOD_DEFINE writes it. Since 1.0.

```c
typedef int (*openrac_mod_load_fn)(const openrac_api* api, openrac_mod* mod);
```

Loads the mod: takes its hook points and callbacks from `api`, and keeps `mod` for the calls
that are its own. Returns 0 to load, non-zero to refuse (after openrac_api.fail gave the
reason). Required. Since 1.0.

```c
typedef void (*openrac_mod_unload_fn)(void);
```

Lets go of what the mod holds, when the program ends. Optional. Since 1.0.

## `openrac_input`

The keyboard and mouse as the port read them for the tick about to run: taken once a tick, after
the window's events and before the game reads its pads (so before the tick's pad reports).
Read it through openrac_api.input; it is the port's, and valid until the next tick.

Since 1.2; the fields from `pointer_x` on are 1.3's, and exist only when `size` reaches them.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `uint32_t size` | sizeof(openrac_input) as the port was built: a newer port's is larger. |
| `uint32_t tick` | Counts the ticks: a new value, a new state. |
| `uint8_t keys[OPENRAC_KEY_COUNT]` | By HID usage: OPENRAC_KEY_HELD \| OPENRAC_KEY_PRESSED. |
| `uint32_t mouse_held` | The OPENRAC_MOUSE_* buttons down now. |
| `uint32_t mouse_pressed` | The OPENRAC_MOUSE_* buttons that went down since the last tick. |
| `float mouse_dx` | The mouse's motion since the last tick, in the system's pixels: raw (no pointer acceleration) while captured; y grows downward. |
| `float mouse_dy` |  |
| `float wheel_x` | The wheel since the last tick, in notches: x > 0 to the right, y > 0 away from the player (up), whatever the system's scroll direction. |
| `float wheel_y` |  |
| `uint8_t focused` | 1 when the game's window has the keyboard; while not, nothing is held. |
| `uint8_t captured` | 1 when the cursor is captured: hidden, kept in the window, motion relative. |
| `uint8_t overlay` | 1 when the port's own overlay or menu has the input now (F3): leave it alone. |
| `uint8_t reserved` | Padding; zero. |
| `float pointer_x` | Since 1.3 (check `size` first): where the cursor is over the game's 4:3 picture, 0..1 across and down (outside it below 0 or above 1), as the game's 2D screen of 512 by 416 pixels has it: x * 512, y * 416 is the game's pixel. Meaningful while the cursor is not captured. |
| `float pointer_y` |  |
| `uint8_t pointer_inside` | Since 1.3: 1 when the cursor is over the picture, in the focused window. |
| `uint8_t reserved2[3]` | Padding; zero. |

While a mod has views (on_views) the port submits to the queue on the game's thread only, so a mod's own use of it there (OpenXR's xrEndFrame) needs no lock. |

## `openrac_view`

One view the port draws in a frame besides the window's: an eye of a headset,
a panel. The mod fills the members up to `image_layout` in
openrac_view_source.begin; the port sets the ones after as it draws.
Since 1.4.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `uint32_t kind` | An OPENRAC_VIEW_* value. |
| `int32_t width` | The picture's size in pixels, each from 1 to 8192. |
| `int32_t height` |  |
| `float position[3]` | The eye relative to the game's camera, in the camera's view space (OpenXR's and OpenGL's: X right, Y up, looking down -Z), in the game's units: a position, and an orientation as a quaternion x, y, z, w. The identity (0 0 0, 0 0 0 1) is the game's own camera; an all-zero orientation counts as the identity. |
| `float orientation[4]` |  |
| `float angle_left` | The field of view as OpenXR's XrFovf gives it: the angles of its left, right, top and bottom edges from straight ahead, in radians (left and down negative). All zero: the game's own vertical one, at the view's shape. |
| `float angle_right` |  |
| `float angle_up` |  |
| `float angle_down` |  |
| `uint32_t texture` | Where the picture goes, in the backend's own terms (openrac_api.graphics), copied as its bytes with no conversion of colour (an sRGB image gets the game's picture as it is shown): - OpenGL: `texture`, a GL_TEXTURE_2D of the port's context, RGBA8 or SRGB8_ALPHA8, at least width by height (an OpenXR swapchain image); - Vulkan: `image`, a VkImage of the port's device, VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM or _SRGB, exactly width by height, usable as a transfer destination, which the port finds in `image_layout` (a VkImageLayout) and leaves in it. Zero and null: the picture is drawn only into the port's own texture (`picture`). |
| `void *image` |  |
| `uint32_t image_layout` |  |
| `uint32_t drawn` | Set by the port: 1 when this frame drew the view anew; 0 when it showed the last frame's picture again (a frame the port draws no world in, as the pause menu's repeated frames), and then that picture is copied again. |
| `uint32_t picture` | Set by the port: its own GL texture holding the view (with OpenGL), until the next frame. |
| `uint32_t reserved[3]` | Padding; zero. |

## `openrac_view_source`

The functions a mod gives on_views. The port copies the structure; `user` is
passed back to each. Every function is called on the game's thread, with the
graphics context current. Since 1.4.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `uint32_t size` | sizeof(openrac_view_source) as the mod was built. |
| `void *user` |  |
| `int (*begin)(void *user, openrac_view *views, int max)` | Called in each frame the port draws the game's scene (each refresh, between the game's ticks too), after the window's picture is recorded: fills views[0] to views[n - 1] (n at most `max`) and returns n; 0 draws none this frame. The place for OpenXR's xrWaitFrame, xrBeginFrame, xrLocateViews and xrAcquireSwapchainImage. Frames that show a movie or a still picture instead of the scene do not call it. |
| `void (*end)(void *user, const openrac_view *views, int count)` | Called once the frame that drew them is submitted to the GPU (after the window's picture is shown), with the views `begin` gave and what the port set in them: the place for xrReleaseSwapchainImage and xrEndFrame. Called after every `begin`, even one that returned 0 or a frame that drew nothing. |
| `void (*closing)(void *user)` | Called once before the graphics context goes (the window closes): let go of everything made with it (OpenXR's session and swapchains). Optional. |

## `openrac_vulkan_setup`

What a mod gives setup_vulkan so that the port's Vulkan device is one the mod
can share (OpenXR's XR_KHR_vulkan_enable2: xrCreateVulkanInstanceKHR,
xrGetVulkanGraphicsDevice2KHR, xrCreateVulkanDeviceKHR). The port copies the
structure; `user` is passed back to each. The functions are called when the
window opens, after openrac_mod_load, on the game's thread: the mod's
manifest says "vulkan_device": true so that it loads before the window.
Pointers stand for the Vulkan types named, and int32_t for VkResult.
Since 1.4.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `uint32_t size` | sizeof(openrac_vulkan_setup) as the mod was built. |
| `void *user` |  |
| `int32_t (*create_instance)(void *user, void *get_instance_proc_addr, const void *create_info, void **instance)` | Makes the instance from `create_info` (a const VkInstanceCreateInfo*, the port's: the extensions and the API version it needs) in place of vkCreateInstance, through `get_instance_proc_addr` (a PFN_vkGetInstanceProcAddr), and sets `*instance`. Returns a VkResult; anything but VK_SUCCESS (0) and the port draws with OpenGL instead. Optional. |
| `void *(*physical_device)(void *user, void *instance)` | Returns the VkPhysicalDevice to draw on, of `instance`; null lets the port choose. The port refuses a device it cannot draw with (and draws with OpenGL instead). Optional. |
| `int32_t (*create_device)(void *user, void *get_instance_proc_addr, void *physical_device, const void *create_info, void **device)` | Makes the device from `create_info` (a const VkDeviceCreateInfo*, the port's) on `physical_device` in place of vkCreateDevice, and sets `*device`. Returns a VkResult, as create_instance. Optional. |

## `openrac_packs_info`

The data packs that change the game in this run (packs_info): gameplay data, collision, a map. A
pack of looks alone is each player's own and is not counted. Since 1.12.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `uint32_t size` | sizeof(openrac_packs_info), set by the caller. |
| `int32_t count` |  |
| `uint32_t digest` | A number that is the same in two games with the same packs in the same order. |

## `openrac_pack_entry`

One data pack (packs_entry). The strings stay valid for the life of the program. Since 1.12.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `uint32_t size` | sizeof(openrac_pack_entry), set by the caller. |
| `const char* id` |  |
| `const char* version` |  |
| `uint32_t digest` |  |
| `const char* name` | The name a player knows it by. Past `size` in an older caller. |

## `openrac_api`

What the port offers a mod. Filled by the port; valid for the life of the program. Every function
is called on the game's thread. Members from "1.2" on are at the end: a mod built for 1.1 never
sees them, and one built for 1.2 loads on a 1.2 port or newer.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `uint32_t size` | sizeof(openrac_api) as the port was built: a newer port's is larger. Since 1.0. |
| `uint16_t api_major` | The port's interface version: at least what the mod was built for, else it is not loaded. Since 1.0. |
| `uint16_t api_minor` |  |
| `const char* game` | The game's id, "rac1" (games/<game>/game.json). Since 1.0. |
| `const char* version` | The disc's version, "pal" or "ntsc". Since 1.0. |
| `const char* openrac_version` | OpenRAC's version, "0.9.0". Since 1.0. |
| `const char* platform` | The platform, "macos-arm64", "linux-x86_64", "windows-x86_64", ... Since 1.0. |
| `uint8_t* memory` | The base of game memory: game address a is memory + a. Fixed for the life of the program. Since 1.0. |
| `void (*log)(openrac_mod* mod, int level, const char* text)` | Writes a line to the session's log, after the mod's id. `level` is an OPENRAC_LOG_* value. Since 1.0. |
| `void (*fail)(openrac_mod* mod, const char* reason)` | Says why the mod refuses to load (status.json and the launcher show it). Only during openrac_mod_load, which then returns non-zero. Since 1.0. |
| `int (*setting_bool)(openrac_mod* mod, const char* key)` | Read the mod's settings (its manifest's "settings"; the values the launcher wrote). A key the manifest does not declare, or of another type, gives 0, 0.0 or "". A string stays valid for the life of the program. Since 1.0. |
| `int64_t (*setting_int)(openrac_mod* mod, const char* key)` |  |
| `double (*setting_float)(openrac_mod* mod, const char* key)` |  |
| `const char* (*setting_string)(openrac_mod* mod, const char* key)` |  |
| `int (*hook)( openrac_mod* mod, const char* name, const char* signature, void* replacement, void** original )` | Takes the hook point `name` (games/<game>.h: its name and signature) for `replacement`, a function of the hook point's signature, which `signature` spells. Sets `*original` to what the replacement goes on to: the game's own function, or the replacement of a mod loaded earlier, so the mod loaded last runs first. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK or one of the other OPENRAC_HOOK_* results. Only during openrac_mod_load. Since 1.0. |
| `int (*on_frame)(openrac_mod* mod, openrac_frame_fn fn, void* user)` | Calls `fn(user)` after each game tick, in load order. Returns 0, or non-zero when refused (after openrac_mod_load). Only during openrac_mod_load. Since 1.0. |
| `int (*on_pad)(openrac_mod* mod, openrac_pad_fn fn, void* user)` | Calls `fn(user, port, report, size)` for each pad report, before the game reads it, in load order. Returns 0, or non-zero when refused (after openrac_mod_load). Only during openrac_mod_load. Since 1.0. |
| `void* (*function)(const char* name)` | Returns a game function by its name in this disc's build ("func_001F9F90" on PAL, "FUN_001f9dc8" on NTSC-U), as a host function to call with its signature; null when there is none. Since 1.0. |
| `void* (*function_at)(openrac_gaddr address)` | Returns the function at a code address, in the level loaded now (a function pointer the game keeps); null when there is none. Since 1.0. |
| `openrac_gaddr (*relocate_data)(openrac_gaddr address)` | Return a global's address for the code loaded now: one of the executable's (guest.h, OPENRAC_DATA), or of level `level`'s program (OPENRAC_LDATA). Ask each time: a level moves its globals. Since 1.0. |
| `openrac_gaddr (*relocate_level_data)(int level, openrac_gaddr address)` |  |
| `int (*loaded_level)(void)` | Returns the level whose program is loaded, -1 for none (the executable's). Since 1.0. |
| `openrac_gaddr (*stack_push)(uint32_t size, openrac_gaddr* saved)` | Gives `size` bytes (aligned to 16) of room on the game's stack for a call that takes the address of a local, and keeps the stack as it was in `*saved`. Returns the room's address. Pair each push with a stack_pop, innermost first. Since 1.0. |
| `void (*stack_pop)(openrac_gaddr saved)` | Gives back what the matching stack_push took: `saved` is what it stored. Since 1.0. |
| `const openrac_input* (*input)(void)` | Returns the keyboard and mouse for the tick about to run. Never null: without a window (a test, a server) nothing is held and nothing moves. Valid until the next tick. Since 1.2. |
| `int (*take_input)(openrac_mod* mod, uint32_t devices)` | Takes `devices` (OPENRAC_INPUT_*) from the port: with OPENRAC_INPUT_KEYBOARD the port's own keyboard table (WASD, Space, ...) no longer presses pad 0's buttons, and the mod presses them through on_pad instead. A gamepad goes on as before; the port's window keys (F3, F11) stay the port's. Returns 0, or OPENRAC_HOOK_TOO_LATE after openrac_mod_load. Since 1.2. |
| `void (*capture_mouse)(openrac_mod* mod, int capture)` | Asks for the cursor captured (`capture` 1: hidden, held in the window, motion relative, as a game's mouse look wants it) or let go (0). Any time; the latest asking of any mod counts. The port lets it go anyway while the window is not focused or its overlay is open, and takes it back when the reason is gone and the mod still asks. Since 1.2. |
| `const openrac_graphics *(*graphics)(void)` | Returns what the port draws with (openrac_graphics). Never null: before the window opens, and without one, its backend is OPENRAC_GRAPHICS_NONE. Any time. Since 1.4. |
| `int (*on_views)(openrac_mod *mod, const openrac_view_source *source)` | Asks the port to draw views of the game besides the window's picture each frame, through `source` (openrac_view_source), with OpenGL and Vulkan. While a mod has views, the Vulkan renderer draws on the game's thread. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, OPENRAC_HOOK_TAKEN when another mod has them, OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for a source without begin or end, or OPENRAC_HOOK_TOO_LATE after openrac_mod_load. Since 1.4. |
| `int (*setup_vulkan)(openrac_mod *mod, const openrac_vulkan_setup *setup)` | Has the port make its Vulkan device through `setup` (openrac_vulkan_setup) when the window opens, so that the mod can share it. Without Vulkan (OpenGL, a build without it) nothing is called. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, OPENRAC_HOOK_TAKEN when another mod has it, OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for a setup too small, or OPENRAC_HOOK_TOO_LATE after openrac_mod_load. Since 1.4. |
| `int (*menu_entry)(openrac_mod* mod, const char* label, openrac_menu_fn fn, void* user)` | Adds an entry named `label` (ASCII, up to 31 characters) to the game's front-end menu, which opens a page of the mod's own: `fn(user, frame)` each frame it is open (openrac_menu_fn). Ratchet & Clank has it in the title's Options list, after the port's own entries (Video, and Planets with developer tools). A game whose front end the port does not know shows none. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for no label or fn or past OPENRAC_MENU_ENTRIES_MAX, or OPENRAC_HOOK_TOO_LATE after openrac_mod_load. Since 1.5. |
| `void (*menu_rect)(openrac_mod* mod, int x, int y, int width, int height, uint32_t rgba)` | Fills the rectangle of `width` by `height` pixels whose top left is (x, y) on the menu page (OPENRAC_MENU_WIDTH by OPENRAC_MENU_HEIGHT) with `rgba` (OPENRAC_RGBA), blended by its alpha; what is outside the page is left out. Only during the mod's own menu callback; ignored otherwise. Since 1.5. |
| `void (*menu_text)(openrac_mod* mod, int x, int y, int size, uint32_t rgba, const char* text)` | Writes `text` (ASCII; a newline starts a line below) on the menu page with its first character's top left at (x, y), each character OPENRAC_MENU_CHAR_WIDTH by OPENRAC_MENU_CHAR_HEIGHT times `size` (1 to 8), in `rgba`. Only during the mod's own menu callback; ignored otherwise. Since 1.5. |
| `int (*on_tick_boundary)(openrac_mod* mod, openrac_tick_boundary_fn fn, void* user)` | Calls `fn(user, tick)` after the game's vertical-blank handlers have run, the port's tick boundary, the only place the savestate calls below are accepted (openrac_tick_boundary_fn). Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_TOO_LATE for no fn or after openrac_mod_load. Since 1.6. |
| `size_t (*savestate_size)(void)` | The byte size of this port build's warm, same-process snapshot; 0 where the running game has none (Ratchet & Clank PAL and NTSC have one). Since 1.6. |
| `int (*savestate_save)(void* out, size_t size)` | Captures a snapshot into `out`, `size` being savestate_size(). Only inside on_tick_boundary; returns 0 on success. The bytes are private to this process and build, not for a cold restore or another version. Since 1.6. |
| `int (*savestate_load)(const void* data, size_t size)` | Restores a snapshot savestate_save made, under the same constraints; returns 0 on success. It may refuse when the runtime allocated new guest statics or strings since the snapshot, because translated call sites cache those addresses in process memory. Since 1.6. |
| `int (*ui_page)(openrac_mod* mod, uint32_t flags, openrac_ui_fn fn, void* user)` | Makes a page of the game's own menus (OPENRAC_UI_OWN_BACK or 0 in `flags`), with nothing on it yet (ui_set), whose events go to `fn(user, page, event)` (openrac_ui_fn). Returns the page's id (0 or more), OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for no fn or past OPENRAC_UI_PAGES_MAX, or OPENRAC_HOOK_TOO_LATE after openrac_mod_load. Since 1.7. |
| `int (*ui_main_item)(openrac_mod* mod, const char* after, const char* label, int page)` | Adds an item named `label` to the title's main menu, after its own item `after` (OPENRAC_UI_NEW_GAME, OPENRAC_UI_LOAD_GAME, OPENRAC_UI_OPTIONS), which opens the mod's `page`. Two after the same item go in the order they were added. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for an unknown `after`, no label, a page that is not the mod's, or past OPENRAC_UI_MAIN_ITEMS_MAX, or OPENRAC_HOOK_TOO_LATE after openrac_mod_load. Since 1.7. |
| `int (*ui_set)(openrac_mod* mod, int page, const openrac_ui_content* content)` | Puts `content` on the mod's `page` (openrac_ui_content), in place of what it had: shown at once if the page is on the screen. Any time. The cursor stays on its item (on the last when there are fewer, and off a TEXT). Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for a page that is not the mod's or no content. Since 1.7. |
| `int (*ui_open)(openrac_mod* mod, int page)` | While one of the mod's pages is on the screen: shows its `page`, a level under a page the main menu opened or in place of one under it; a page that is on a level above goes back to it. OPENRAC_UI_GO_BACK goes back a level, as Triangle does. Since 1.9 also while the title's main menu itself is on the screen: shows the page one of the mod's main-menu items opens (openrac_api.ui_main_item), as choosing the item does, so a mod brings the player back to its page after a game it ended. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN when none of the mod's pages (nor the main menu, for an item's page) is on the screen or the page is not the mod's. Since 1.7. |
| `int (*ui_confirm)(openrac_mod* mod, int page, const char* question, uint32_t tag)` | While the mod's `page` is on the screen: asks `question` with the game's prompt box in place of the list, the footer saying Cross is yes and Triangle no; the answer is an OPENRAC_UI_ANSWER with `tag`. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN when the page is not on the screen or another question is open. Since 1.7. |
| `int (*ui_cursor)(openrac_mod* mod, int page, int item)` | Returns the item under the cursor of the mod's `page` (-1 for a page that is not the mod's), after moving it to `item` when that is 0 or more and an item the cursor takes. Since 1.7. |
| `int (*ui_sound)(openrac_mod* mod, int sound)` | Plays one of the game's menu sounds (OPENRAC_UI_SOUND_*) while one of the mod's pages is on the screen. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN otherwise. Since 1.7. |
| `int (*play_status)(openrac_play_status* out)` | Fills `out` (its size set) with what the game is doing: its phase (OPENRAC_PLAY_*), its level. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for a game the port knows no play of (phase OPENRAC_PLAY_NONE). Since 1.8. |
| `const char* (*level_name)(int level)` | The name of the game's level `level` ("Veldin"), or null for none. Since 1.8. |
| `int (*hero_pose)(openrac_pose* out)` | Fills `out` (its size set) with the hero's pose as it is drawn now. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN when there is no hero (no level, the hero not placed yet). Since 1.8. |
| `int (*figure_create)(openrac_mod* mod)` | Makes a figure in the level: a moby that looks like the hero, in his pose, drawn but never running his logic, colliding with nothing and targeted by nothing, until figure_remove or the level goes (a new play_status.loads). Returns its id (0 or more), or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN outside a level, past OPENRAC_FIGURES_MAX, or when the level has no room for a moby. Since 1.8. |
| `int (*figure_pose)(openrac_mod* mod, int id, const openrac_pose* pose)` | Puts the mod's figure `id` in `pose`: where it is, its rotation and scale, and its animation (a new seq blends into it; the figure animates by itself, at anim_speed nudged faster or slower to keep to the pose's key and anim_time, and is put on the key only when more than a few keys away). Each tick the mod wants it to move. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for a figure that is not the mod's or is gone with its level (then the mod makes another). Since 1.8. |
| `int (*figure_remove)(openrac_mod* mod, int id)` | Takes the mod's figure `id` out of the level. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for one that is not the mod's (gone already). Since 1.8. |
| `int (*play_start)(openrac_mod* mod, int level, const void* save, size_t size)` | From the front end (phase OPENRAC_PLAY_FRONT_END): starts a game, after this frame, as the title's New Game and Load Game do: with `save` null a new game in `level` (0 the first); otherwise the `size` bytes of `save` (a save as save_read or save_capture give it), which continue in its own level, or in `level` when that is 0 or more. Nothing is written to the memory card. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, OPENRAC_HOOK_TAKEN while a start or travel asked before is still to happen, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN outside the front end, for a level the game has not, or a save it does not take. Since 1.8. |
| `int (*play_travel)(openrac_mod* mod, int level)` | In a level with the player in control (phase OPENRAC_PLAY_PLAYING), and since 1.9 also in its scenes and menus (OPENRAC_PLAY_SCENE, OPENRAC_PLAY_MENU: a cutscene, the pause menu, a vendor): leaves it for `level`, after this frame, as the ship's travel does (the flight between planets, then the level); -1 goes back to the title, as the pause menu's Quit Game does (since 1.9). Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, OPENRAC_HOOK_TAKEN while a start or travel is still to happen, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN otherwise. Since 1.8. |
| `size_t (*save_capture)(void* out, size_t size)` | The game's progress now, as a save (the memory card's save file's bytes): written to `out` when `size` is large enough. Returns its size in bytes (call with a null `out` to ask), or 0 when there is none (no game started). Since 1.8. |
| `int (*save_slot)(int slot, openrac_save_info* out)` | Fills `out` (its size set) with what the memory card's save `slot` holds. Returns 1 for a save, 0 for an empty slot (or one the game would not load), -1 past the game's last slot. Since 1.8. |
| `size_t (*save_read)(int slot, void* out, size_t size)` | The bytes of the memory card's save `slot`, for play_start: written to `out` when `size` is large enough. Returns their size, or 0 for no save there. Since 1.8. |
| `int (*moby_list)(openrac_moby* out, int max)` | Fills `out` with the level's live mobys and its placed ones deleted (OPENRAC_MOBY_DEAD), at most `max` of them (each one's size set by the port), in slot order, whatever menu is up. Returns how many there are (more than `max`: the rest left out); 0 outside a level. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*moby_slot)(int key)` | Returns the slot of the placed moby `key`, or -1 for none (killed, or no such record). Since 1.9. |
| `int (*moby_drive)(openrac_mod* mod, int slot, int on)` | Drives the moby in `slot` (`on` 1: its update no longer runs, the mod poses it) or lets it go (0). A drive ends with its level. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for no moby there, or OPENRAC_HOOK_TAKEN when another mod drives it. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*moby_pose)(openrac_mod* mod, int slot, const openrac_moby* pose)` | Puts the moby in `slot` in the pose `pose` gives (its position, rotation, scale when above 0, and animation, as figure_pose does). Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for no moby there. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*moby_kill)(openrac_mod* mod, int slot)` | Deletes the moby in `slot` as the game deletes one (a placed one stays dead until its level loads again). Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*moby_spawn)(openrac_mod* mod, int oclass, const openrac_moby* pose)` | Makes a moby of class `oclass` (one the level has) in `pose`, driven by the mod. Returns its slot, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN (no level, no room, a class the level has not). Since 1.9. |
| `int (*figure_slot)(openrac_mod* mod, int id)` | Returns the slot of the mod's figure `id` (figure_create), or of the hero's moby with -1; -1 for none. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*on_moby_update)(openrac_mod* mod, openrac_moby_update_fn fn, void* user)` | Calls `fn(user, slot, phase)` around each moby's update (openrac_moby_update_fn). One mod's. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, OPENRAC_HOOK_TAKEN when another mod has it, or OPENRAC_HOOK_TOO_LATE after openrac_mod_load. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*hero_stand_in)(openrac_mod* mod, const float position[3], int figure)` | Only in the gate's call before an update: for that update the hero is at `position`, and his moby is the mod's figure `figure` (-1: his own), as another player would be there; put back after it. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN outside that call. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*on_moby_hit)(openrac_mod* mod, openrac_hit_fn fn, void* user)` | Calls `fn(user, &hit)` for each hit the game posts (openrac_hit_fn). One mod's. Returns as on_moby_update. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*moby_hit)(openrac_mod* mod, const openrac_hit* hit)` | Posts `hit` to its victim as the game posts one (the victim's update reads it: an enemy takes the damage, the hero is hurt), not told to on_moby_hit. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for no victim there. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*play_eyes)(openrac_mod* mod, const float* xyz, int count)` | Sets up to OPENRAC_EYES_MAX points (x, y, z each) besides the camera: the mobys within their update distance of one run too (the world near other players). `count` 0 clears them. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*bolts)(int add)` | Adds `add` to the player's bolts (0: none) and returns them. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*play_overlay_pause)(openrac_mod* mod, int on)` | While `on` (1), the level's mobys keep being updated under the game's pause menu and its freeze dialogs, in the level's own mobys (the hero stays as the menu left it, and the picture goes on as play_live_picture says): a game that plays with others never stops their world for a menu. 0: as the game does. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for a game without it. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*moby_slot_of)(openrac_gaddr moby)` | Returns the slot of the moby at game address `moby` (a hook point's argument), -1 for none. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*play_skip)(openrac_mod* mod)` | Skips the scene playing (a cutscene, the ship's landing or take-off, the flight between planets) the way the game's own skip does, as Start does with the port's "Skip cutscenes": for the next ticks, until the scene is over. For a party whose scenes end together. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for a game the port has no skip of. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*hero_held)(openrac_held* out)` | Fills `out` (its size set) with what the hero wears and holds now (openrac_held), the pieces in the game's slot order. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN when there is no hero (as hero_pose) or the port knows no pieces of the game. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*figure_held)(openrac_mod* mod, int id, const openrac_held* held)` | Has the mod's figure `id` wear and hold `held`: each piece a moby of its class on the figure's joint (a loose one where it says), animated as it says, made when the level has its class loaded or can load it beside the hero's own (a piece it cannot have is left out, the hand's falling back to the wrench), taken off when left out of a later call, with the figure or with its level. Call it each tick the figure is posed. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for a figure that is not the mod's or is gone. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*hero_shots)(openrac_shot* out, int max)` | The shots the hero fired since the last call (any mod's), oldest first: at most `max` into `out` (each one's size set by the port), at most OPENRAC_SHOTS_MAX kept between calls. Returns how many were written. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*figure_shot)(openrac_mod* mod, int id, const openrac_shot* shot)` | Has the mod's figure `id` fire `shot` as the hero would: the game's own projectile and its effects, owned by the figure, hitting and breaking nothing in this game (the shooter's game tells what it hit). Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for a figure that is not the mod's, or a weapon the port cannot fire for a figure. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*play_notice)(openrac_mod* mod, const char* text)` | Shows `text` (one line, UTF-8) at the top of the game's picture until the mod shows another or clears it (null or ""): what the game's own words cannot say, such as a party waiting for its players. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*ui_pause_item)(openrac_mod* mod, const char* label, int page)` | Adds an item named `label` to the Options page of the pause menu in a level, after the game's own items (and the port's Video), which opens the mod's `page` (ui_page). Ratchet & Clank: the page is a copy of the game's Camera options page, its title the page's and its list a row per item, the label on the left and a choice's value on the right, a few rows at a time; the game's cursor, sounds and Triangle (back to Options, but for OPENRAC_UI_OWN_BACK and while a question is open, which Triangle answers no); a question (ui_confirm) is the title with two rows, Yes and No; the footer is the game's. ui_open swaps another of the mod's pages into its place, ui_cursor only reads the cursor and ui_sound plays nothing there. Two go in the order they were added. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN for no label, a page that is not the mod's, or past OPENRAC_UI_PAUSE_ITEMS_MAX, or OPENRAC_HOOK_TOO_LATE after openrac_mod_load. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*scene_playing)(int* frame)` | The in-level scene playing now: a cutscene of the level's own, which the game starts from the level's mobys (a person spoken to, a place reached, a level's opening) or play_scene started; not a movie, a slideshow, the ship's landing and take-off, or a scene the pause menu plays again for its player. Returns its number in the level (the game's own, the same in every game of that level), or -1 with none playing; `frame` (when not null) gets how many of the scene's frames have played. Since 1.9. |
| `int (*play_scene)(openrac_mod* mod, int scene)` | Starts the level's scene `scene` (scene_playing's number) as the game's own trigger does, from its start: its actors made, its camera, sound and music, the hero held until it ends (or is skipped: play_skip). It starts at the end of a tick with the player in control in the level (OPENRAC_PLAY_PLAYING, the hero alive); asked before that (a menu up, another scene playing), the request waits, until it starts, the level is left or loaded again, or another call replaces it (-1 drops it). For a party whose games play the same scenes. Returns OPENRAC_HOOK_OK, or OPENRAC_HOOK_UNKNOWN outside a level, or for a game the port starts no scenes of. Since 1.9. |
